title: Trotterization with Many-body Coulomb Interactions: Convergence for General Initial Conditions and State-Dependent Improvements
summary: Efficiently simulating many-body quantum systems with Coulomb interactions is a fundamental question in quantum physics, quantum chemistry, and quantum computing, yet it presents unique challenges: the Hamiltonian is an unbounded operator; its Hilbert space dimension grows exponentially with particle number; and the Coulomb potential is singular, long-ranged, and non-smooth, violating the regularity assumptions of many prior state-of-the-art many-body simulation analyses. In this work, we establish rigorous error bounds for Trotter formulas applied to these systems. Our first main result…
